score.meaning: Strong, coherent authored visual storytelling with a concrete subject and an economical return to the visitor. The number rates inspected setup/payoff structure and rendered staging, not the still-unobserved felt rhythm or audience success. The two named deductions concern how distinctly the payoff reads and how literally attention connects to its subject on phones.

strengths: The question gives the attention a cause. The final desktop stage places What should software remember? to screen-right, matching the authored initial gaze. It is a question with an invitation to explore, not an unsupported result or victory claim.

The investigation has an intentional lead/support order: antenna at 150 ms, gaze at 330 ms, head/glasses at 790 ms, a gathered hand and lower scan at 1190 ms, an identical-pose consideration hold at 1610–1900 ms, return toward the visitor at 2350 ms, and the small offer at 2720 ms. The whole body does not compete for attention throughout.

The selected warm ending is held through the finite 4100 ms completion. The static cue stays available, so completing or skipping playback does not remove the project context. This is a complete thought with breathing room rather than a compulsory loop.

The final portrait composition gives the original little hand and face enough display area to inspect at 390 px. The paired day/night rendered images retain the same soft head, short body, small mittens, attached feet, unequal antennae and layered wings.

One-peek is a useful controlled economy study: the opening is shared with the two-peek control, but the conceal-and-recheck beat is removed while the asymmetric held eye remains. The decoded sheet makes that structural difference inspectable without pretending to resolve which timing is funnier.

The wry study confines its extra event to an afterthought after the shared invitation; source preserves the common opening. Nag's selected Investigate & share remains the lead, so the optional study does not redefine the intended personality.

Playback begins on request, remains pausable/scrubbable, and reduced motion retains a chosen pose and the complete visible question. Those choices keep intentional character performance available without making it an obstacle to the content.

deductions.name: The presenting payoff has limited silhouette separation
deductions.severity: moderate craft weakness, nonblocking for this local study
deductions.confidence: medium-high for the inspected stills; unmeasured at normal speed
deductions.basis: At the 2720 ms endpoint the presenting mitten remains close to the ruff and screen-right forewing. In curious-investigate.png and the smaller exact-engine sheet, the glasses and head change dominate the read; the final offer is a relatively small change from the gathered consideration pose. The larger final 390 px stage improves visibility but does not fully separate the hand's meaning from a general friendly raised hand.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Compare the exact 1190/1900/2350/2720 ms sequence at the intended display size without the intent explanation. If the presentation is still ambiguous, audition only a small existing-wrist position/rotation change or a clearer head-before-hand handoff; retain tiny mitten dimensions and the same numeric poses in both themes. Do not enlarge the anatomy to buy clarity.

deductions.name: Portrait staging weakens the literal attention-to-question relationship
deductions.confidence: high for the layout difference; medium for its storytelling consequence
deductions.basis: The desktop scene puts the question beside the moth, close to the authored screen-right gaze and offering direction. At 390 px the question occupies a tall block above the character, while the authored reading scan turns right and then lower. Both elements are visible together in the scrolled stage capture, but their causal relationship relies more on the copy and sequence context. The 320 px initial-viewport capture does not yet show the figure and cannot establish the complete 320 px scene relationship.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Inspect the whole 320 px and 390 px scene during the notice/read/return beats. A future layout audition should strengthen the question's placement relative to the unchanged gaze before introducing new pose logic. Preserve readable copy and the increased character display size.

improvementCriteria: Confirm the handoff from consideration to invitation at normal playback speed, then use the frames to diagnose a named ambiguity. A source timeline alone is not sufficient evidence to retime the performance.
Review matched complete phone scenes at the actual intended display sizes so the relationship between question, eyes and hand can be judged together.
Retain the finite hold, static project cue, identical light/dark numeric poses and tiny anatomy while investigating the two craft weaknesses.

Keep the one-peek/two-peek and warm/wry comparisons controlled; do not promote a timing preference to a claim of audience comprehension or personal fit. Nag's warm selection already resolves the personal-fit lead.

No physical-phone, screen-reader speech, or new unprimed-human observation. Desktop/emulated evidence and AI craft judgment do not establish those outcomes.
The viewed 320 px screenshot proves the visible initial layout and heading wrap, not the complete scrolled composition or interaction.
The full 24-emotion film was not watched; its metadata and the all-final held-pose sheet were inspected. A catalogue is not an authored continuous story.
The geometry evidence reports 567 matched input samples with no mismatches; that is supplied numeric/rendered attribute evidence, not a new comprehensive geometry test performed by this reviewer.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: The requested 4.1-second character investigation is intentional explanatory content with cause, consideration and an invitation. Those UI budgets apply to controls and navigation, not to compressing the whole scene.

Immediate keyboard feedback is appropriate for the interface, but keyboard activation of Play must still provide the deliberately requested performance. Removing that access would contradict the product purpose.
